# PasswordBox

Header: `winui/ui/text/PasswordBox.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/text/PasswordBox.hpp`.

A single-line field that masks what is typed into it.

It owns a [`TextBox`](text-box.md#uitextbox) as its edit part, masked with [`password_char()`](#password_char). Caret, selection, clipboard and context menu work on the hidden text. A password offers no Cut or Copy, is never spell checked, and screen readers get only mask characters. In the default `PasswordBoxRevealMode::Peek`, a reveal button shows the password while it is held. The button shows only for a password typed since the field was last empty, so whoever sits down next can't peek at a password filled in earlier. In a spec tree it is built by [`ui::PasswordBox`](#uipasswordbox).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::PasswordBox> box;
window.set_content(ui::PasswordBox{
    .header           = "Password",
    .placeholder_text = "Enter your password",
    .max_length       = 64,
    .width            = 300.0f,
    .on_password_changed = [&box](const std::string& password) {
        if (password == "Password")
            box->set_password(""); // rejecting a value from inside the handler is fine
    },
    .control = box,
});

// Imperatively:
auto pin = std::make_unique<ui::PasswordBoxControl>();
pin->set_password_char(U'*');
pin->set_reveal_mode(ui::PasswordBoxRevealMode::Hidden);
pin->on_password_changed([](const std::string& p) { /* validate p */ });
```

## `ui::PasswordBox`

A field for a password: the text is masked, and can be peeked at with the reveal button. Builds a [ui::PasswordBoxControl](#uipasswordboxcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
void sign_in(const std::string& password); // the app's own
std::string secret;

window.set_content(ui::PasswordBox{
    .header              = "Password",
    .placeholder_text    = "Enter your password",
    .max_length          = 64,
    .width               = 240,
    .on_password_changed = [&](const std::string& p) { secret = p; },
    .on_submit           = [&] { sign_in(secret); },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::PasswordBox{
    .header, .description, .error, .placeholder_text, .password, .max_length, .password_char,
    .reveal_mode, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled,
    .accessibility, .on_password_changed, .on_submit, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited,
    .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

### handle_context_menu

```cpp
bool handle_context_menu(std::optional<Point> position, ContextMenuHost& host) override
```

Window::handle_context_menu() calls this on the focused element when the user right-clicks or presses Shift+F10/the Menu key, after focusing whatever focusable element sits under the pointer, as a pointer Down would. `position` is the right-click point (window-client DIPs), or nullopt for a keyboard request, where the element picks its own anchor ([TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox): its caret). `host` is only valid for this call, so show a menu through it here or not at all. Returns whether a menu was shown; default: none.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

### hit_test_children

```cpp
void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children `p` (in this element's layout coordinates) is tested against, topmost first. Default: what [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) lists, last first. A container that draws in another order ([Panel](../layout/panel.md#uipanel)'s z-index), a control with parts [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) does not list, or one whose parts cover others in places (a pane drawn over the content) lists them here.

### covers_children_at

```cpp
bool covers_children_at(Point p) const override
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

This element's own part of clear_dirty(): clear any part it owns but leaves out of [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) (a parked page, a hidden button), through that part's clear_dirty(). Default: nothing.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

This element's own part of [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick): a clock of its own ([ToolTip](tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay, an animation's phase, a caret blink). Runs after the visual layer has advanced and before the children are ticked, which [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick) does by itself. Tick only parts that [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) does not list here. Default: nothing.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

## Enumerations

### PasswordBoxRevealMode

```cpp
enum class PasswordBoxRevealMode
```

How a [ui::PasswordBox](#uipasswordbox) shows its password.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Peek` | Masked, with a reveal button that shows the password while held down (the default). The button appears only while the box is focused, for a password typed since the box was last empty. |
| `Hidden` | Always masked; no reveal button. |
| `Visible` | Always shown in clear text; no reveal button. |
